specification.objective: Refine the mobile workspace header brand block so the menu trigger is grouped with the TouchIn mark and wordmark, with a rounded yellow background and a contrasting menu icon.

requirements.statement: Below the existing 1080 px responsive breakpoint, the hamburger menu button is inside the same yellow brand block as the TouchIn fingerprint mark and wordmark, positioned before the mark.
The mobile brand block has rounded corners and retains the existing accent-yellow background.
The hamburger icon uses the theme's onPrimary foreground for contrast on the yellow block, distinct from the prior onSurface icon color.
Tapping the hamburger continues to invoke the existing drawer-open callback; the desktop layout and drawer behavior remain unchanged.

acceptance_criteria.statement: At mobile width, the menu button is a descendant of the yellow brand block and precedes the fingerprint mark and TOUCHIN wordmark.
The brand block uses AppTheme.accent with a non-zero rounded corner radius, and the menu icon foreground equals ColorScheme.onPrimary.
The existing drawer open/close animation test and affected workspace shell tests continue to pass.

invariants.statement: The shared 1080 px breakpoint, desktop navigation, mobile destination label, and drawer open/close interaction remain unchanged.
No new dependencies or backend, authentication, authorization, route, API, or data changes are introduced.

forbidden_states.statement: The hamburger button remains outside the yellow brand block or uses the old surface foreground against the yellow background.
The mobile yellow brand block has square corners or the desktop navigation layout changes.

inputs.statement: A mobile viewport below 1080 px, the current color theme, and activation of the hamburger menu button.

outputs.statement: A rounded accent-yellow mobile brand block containing the contrasting menu button, fingerprint mark, and TouchIn wordmark.

failure_semantics.statement: On the locked baseline, the focused mobile brand test fails because the hamburger button is outside the brand block.

argv: mobile header puts the contrasting menu inside the rounded brand block
mobile header puts the contrasting menu inside the rounded brand block
